design_rationale:
DESIGN RATIONALE / WORKLOG - task 0 (project_waitlist_reservations, env_0082) - revision 2

0. DRAW (scripts/draw_counts.py --task 0, fixed): prerequisite_problems=1, factor_counts=[5, 4]. Root waitlist_ext_relocation_offer_estimate takes 5, prerequisite waitlist_ext_relocation_restore_size takes 4.

1. WHY THIS IS A GOOD TEST. Ruth Fairweather (moved from Minneapolis to Saugerties NY) asks only "can I get my share at Esopus Creek now?". Capacity is open (Esopus Creek unallocated_kw 14.60) and her Relocation Priority reservation 3a271876-5b47-4517-99d9-0f51dec17ff6 is the only queued reservation on the project, so the offer is owed (state_due). The agent must (a) read the offer policy's prerequisite sentence ("A Relocation Priority offer and its estimate are fixed only after the reservation's requested kW is no more than the restored size of the household's closed share."), (b) work the restored size out of her closed Minnesota share (1cd2e523-3a49-46e6-b683-94b6a275ba45: Commit 5, 13.00 kW, right-sized by 2.00 kW at its 2026-04-20 true-up, which also recorded a production-guarantee shortfall; closed moved_out_of_territory 2026-07-01) and her Woodstock cabin share on the same project (a15c10f1-eca2-4636-96d5-be39e79689d5: Commit 10, 4.00 kW), (c) explain it so she submits the lowering herself (owner=user tool) and (d) price the full offer from the cabin share's own record. Difficulty comes from reconciling two charters (waitlist + home ledgers: statements, reversals, true-ups with guarantees and resizes, filings), not from tool choice.

2. SCOPE / HEADROOM. Task 0 claims the Relocation Priority class only: the restore change (set_relocation_request_cdb5c762, user) and the relocation offer (extend_relocation_offer_f94b15ad, agent). Task 1 holds the Residential Standard and Residential Add-On classes (their own fit and offer tools). The restore's scope requires the request so set to be within the account headroom of waitlist_agg_account_headroom (the Saugerties account: no other open share, usage 19500 kWh as of 2026-09 -> headroom 16.9 kW), so the restore never has to state a headroom term of its own.

3. DSL DECISION. The DSL cannot read projects or utility_accounts, so no extended figure rests on expected_yield_kwh_per_kw, est_credit_rate_per_kwh, commercial_operation_date or annual_usage_kwh. Both policies are scoped to the case where the household holds a share on the offered project, whose statements and true-ups carry that array's actual output, credit value and (through a guarantee-assessed true-up) its design output; every other case stays under the base rule verbatim (self-naming kWh and savings overwrites with sibling tails). No offered_kw overwrite: the prerequisite sentence is the only statement of the dependency, and the base offered_kw clause holds unchanged once the request is restored.

4. FACTOR CARD.
 waitlist_ext_relocation_restore_size (computes requested_kw = 10.8; all-baseline 14.4). Order sentence: replacement of the prior output, then its floor, then the kept-share multiplier; replacement of the restore yield; then the restored size, then the sizing step.
  - prior_output_history (method): latest closed-share true-up 2026-04-20 completed fewer than twelve whole months before closed_date 2026-07-01 -> its credited_kwh_12m 14608; standard (statements posted in the last 15 whole months = 15424 kWh) -> 11.3.
  - prior_output_guarantee_floor (parameter, R5 basis): that true-up shortfall 199, contract year 2 none -> floor at half of (14608 + 14807) = 14707.5; no floor -> 10.7.
  - kept_share_of_output (method): that true-up recorded resize_kw 2.00 -> x 11.00/(11.00+2.00) = 0.846154; x1 -> 12.7.
  - restore_yield_basis (parameter): cabin true-up 2026-04-15 assessed a guarantee -> design output per kW 4140/4.00/0.90 = 1150; twelve-month output per kW 4268/4.00 -> 11.6.
  plain: raw 14707.5 x 0.846154 / 1150 = 10.8216 -> 10.8 (increment_kw 0.1); lesser of 16.00 and 10.8.
 waitlist_ext_relocation_offer_estimate (computes estimated_annual_savings = 181.32; all-baseline 173.86). Order sentence: output replacement, floor, per-kW, blend, kWh rounding; value replacement, then trend.
  - output_history_basis (method): cabin true-up 2026-04-15 within 12 whole months -> 4003 kWh; standard twelve-month 4268 -> 185.41.
  - guarantee_output_floor (parameter): shortfall in both contract years (137 and 150) -> floor at the latest guaranteed_kwh 4140; none -> 176.93.
  - young_share_blend (parameter, MULTI-SOURCE: line count AND assessed guarantee): 32 posted lines -> 0.75 x 1035 + 0.25 x design 1150 = 1063.75; unblended -> 176.41.
  - credit_value_recency (method): true-up 6 whole months ago and net kWh since -> 366.04/2843 = 0.128751; twelve-month 536.58/4268 -> 177.05.
  - credit_rate_trend (parameter, R6): contract-year-1 true-up 18 whole months ago -> x 0.1236/0.1210 = 1.021488 (inside 0.95-1.05); x1 -> 177.51.
  plain: offered kW = requested_kw 10.80 (after the change); kWh = RND(10.80 x 1063.75 x 1) = 11489; savings = RND(11489 x 0.131518 x 12/100) = 181.32.
 Every factor is cross-difficulty (home). The relocation offer declares no banked-credit ladder and its rule carries none (no undeclared ladder).

5. FACTOR-READS TABLE (each factor's own bindings; no factor reads another factor's binding): prior_output_history -> closed true-up credited_kwh_12m / review_date, closed statements (count, all-history net); prior_output_guarantee_floor -> closed true-ups shortfall_kwh (latest and contract year before), guaranteed_kwh; kept_share_of_output -> closed true-up resize_kw, move_removal and subscriber_increase filings; restore_yield_basis -> cabin true-up guaranteed_kwh, review_date, credited_kwh_12m; output_history_basis -> cabin all-history statements (with the base true-up reads); guarantee_output_floor -> cabin true-ups shortfall_kwh (latest and contract year before); young_share_blend -> cabin posted-line count, design output per kW (true-up guaranteed_kwh, allocation, plan guarantee pct); credit_value_recency -> cabin statements posted since review_date; credit_rate_trend -> cabin contract-year-before true-up avg_credit_rate / review_date.

6. DEFINING-SENTENCE TABLE: restored size / prior output / restore yield / request set -> restore B1-B4; whole months -> restore and offer month sentences; order -> each policy's order sentence; floor, kept share, yield, history, blend, recency, trend -> each factor's own sentence; annual output figure / output per kW / credit value per kWh / estimates -> offer B1-B6; design output per kW -> young_share_blend (restore_yield_basis repeats its own words).

7. PAIRWISE METHOD-TIER TABLE (B1): output_history_basis T1 review credited_kwh_12m / T2 all-history net x12 / line count / T3 fixed twelve-month window - review row vs line count vs window. credit_value_recency T1 review avg_credit_rate / T2 window selected by review_date / T3 twelve-month window - review row vs data-selected window. prior_output_history T1 review credited / T2 annualized all history / T3 window set by closed_date. kept_share_of_output T1 removal over removal + resize_kw / T2 removal over removal less increase filings / T3 x1 - review field vs filings. Parameter tiers select distinct values (floor: guaranteed vs midpoint vs none; trend: ratio vs half-damped ratio vs 1; yield: design vs review actual vs window actual).

8. PROBES (scratch copies, probe_r2.py): decoy second closed share with closure_reason subscriber_cancellation -> restore unchanged (closure_reason filter); decoy notice_given share on the project -> unchanged (status filter); closed share without true-ups -> standard / no floor / x1 tiers, no error; closed share contract year 2 also short -> floor tier 1 (same rounded size); cabin share without true-up -> yield standard; cabin true-up without assessed guarantee -> yield tier 2; offer: decoy closed prior share on the project -> unchanged; no contract-year-1 true-up -> floor tier 2 and trend x1; no true-ups -> standard tiers; reversal inside the since-review window -> net reading moves the value per kWh. Out of scope by rule words: two active shares on the project, no statement posted in twelve whole months, restored size below min_requested_kw or above the headroom.

9. TRIGGER LIST: extend_relocation_offer_f94b15ad writes waitlist_offer_extended (triggers waitlist:waitlist_offer_made only) and waitlist_offer_made (triggers []); set_relocation_request_cdb5c762 writes waitlist_request_updated (triggers []). No write lands in another category; waitlist_offer_accepted is never written.

10. PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root waitlist_ext_relocation_offer_estimate <- value_input, form state, gate offered_kw, sentence quoted above, condition 'requested_kw no more than the restored size', resolved_by set_relocation_request_cdb5c762 (owner user). False at the opening: requested_kw 16.0 vs restored 10.8. Exactly one write in this difficulty lowers a Relocation Priority request (the task-1 tools act on other classes). Four-point test: connective 'only after'; record-visible state; no tool/policy/code token; hard strength. Deletion sensitivity: skipping the change gives offered_kw 16.00 and savings 268.61. user_scenario names no prerequisite; tools validate formats only.

11. BASE-INVARIANT CARD. Offer: waitlist_evt_offer_terms.offered_only (the offer tool sets offered and records the row in one call); waitlist_queue_order (queued, no higher class queued on Esopus Creek, no unanswered offer); headroom 10.80 x 1150 = 12420 kWh <= 19500 kWh (usage as of 2026-09). respond_by_date = 2026-10-26 + 14 = 2026-11-09. Change: waitlist_request_changes (queued; a decrease keeps queue_date) and the headroom. temporal_feasibility [].

12. SEED NOTES. Home charges = credit_value x (100 - savings_rate_pct)/100 half-up, invoiced 5 days after posting, due 21 days later; closed share dual-billed and paid by ACH three days before due; cabin share consolidated, utility remittance 12 days after invoice; the reversed December 2025 cabin line is offset by a credit_reversal_correction before its remittance. True-ups follow the home true-up rule: guaranteed_kwh = allocation x 1340 | 1150 x pct; closed CY3 shortfall 199 -> guarantee credit, resize 2.00 (expected 17420 above 115 percent of usage 14800; largest 0.1-kW share within 100 percent = 11.0); cabin CY1 and CY2 shortfalls -> guarantee credits on their review dates. Closed share: ETF waived (moved_out_of_territory); June 2026 statement posted after closing is priced normally. Reservation submitted 2026-07-09 (within 90 days of closing), queue_date = submitted_date, reconfirm_due 2027-01-09; no notice is due before frozen_time (first position notice and the reconfirmation notice fall after it).

13. REALISM TAGS. R3: annualizing short histories, whole-month windows. R5: production-guarantee floor (guaranteed_kwh as recorded); restore of the share given up measured in output and converted at the project's design yield (the yield home_agg_account_sizing sizes by). R6 (waivable, keyed on recorded true-ups, catalogue in worklog): young-share blend weights, half-way floor for a single shortfall year, credit-rate trend with a 5 percent band. No company factor moves a utility credit value.

14. STANDARD SOLUTION + VERIFICATION. Reads: customer, verify (phone + ZIP), reservations, utility accounts, Esopus Creek, queue on the project, home subscriptions, closed-share reviews/credits/allocations/billing/requests, Crow River, cabin reviews/credits/allocations/billing; unlock+call set_relocation_request_cdb5c762 (10.8) by Ruth; unlock+call extend_relocation_offer_f94b15ad (10.80 kW, Meadowlark Commit 5, 11489 kWh, 181.32, 2026-11-09). Verification by check_compute's own build_env/eval_compute (evalpol.py): restore {'result': 10.8, 'prior_output_history': 11.3, 'prior_output_guarantee_floor': 10.7, 'kept_share_of_output': 12.7, 'restore_yield_basis': 11.6, 'ALL_BASELINE': 14.4}; offer {'result': 181.32, 'output_history_basis': 185.41, 'guarantee_output_floor': 176.93, 'young_share_blend': 176.41, 'credit_value_recency': 177.05, 'credit_rate_trend': 177.51, 'ALL_BASELINE': 173.86}. Gates 7/7 OK on the final form.

15. DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT. Restore: max(14608, (14608 + 14807)/2) x 11/13 / (4140/4/0.9) = 10.82 -> 10.8 kW. Offer: (0.75 x 4140/4 + 0.25 x 1150) x 10.80 = 11488.5 -> 11489 kWh; 366.04/2843 x 0.1236/0.1210 x 12 percent x 11489 = 181.32. Same as gold.

16. REVISIONS. Round 1: factor bindings carry their own reads; null FK ids; every seeded row read. Round 2 (policy audit): restore window stated once; order sentences; headroom moved into the restore scope; unreal guaranteed-output sizing and share-keyed wear removed; guarantee floor tier 2 made live (single-shortfall midpoint) and mirrored on the closed share; restore yield by record and credit-rate trend added; the size-band step retired; offered_kw overwrite removed; tool bodies enforce every docstring format; world re-tuned and every seeded row re-priced.
user_scenario:
You are Ruth Fairweather, a 64-year-old retired school librarian who moved this summer from Minneapolis to a house in Saugerties, New York. You speak warmly and a little hurriedly, and you like to get to the point. Back in Minnesota you had a Meadowlark solar share that you had to give up when you moved, and in July you put your name on Meadowlark's relocation priority list for the Esopus Creek project, asking for 16 kilowatts because the new house is bigger. A neighbor mentioned that Esopus Creek has opened up some space, so you are calling to ask: can I get my share at Esopus Creek now? You would like the representative to take care of it on this call.
When the representative asks you to confirm who you are, you say your phone number is 6515550163 (you kept your Minnesota number) and your ZIP code is 12477; only if they still need something more, your date of birth is 1962-05-21. You don't know any account or reservation numbers and say they can look them up. If they ask about other Meadowlark accounts, you mention that you still have a small share for your cabin in Woodstock and that the old Minnesota share was closed when you moved.
You don't know how Meadowlark sizes shares. If the representative explains that the relocation list only restores the size of the share you gave up and that your request has to come down to that size before an offer can go out, you agree right away - you would rather have the share now - and tell them to set it to whatever that restored size is. When they hand you the change to submit yourself, you submit it with exactly the size they give you; if they ask whether you would rather keep the 16 kilowatts and wait, you say no.
When the representative tells you an offer has been made and gives you its size, plan, estimated first-year savings and the date you need to answer by, you thank them, say you will read the offer letter and answer before that date, and end the call; you do not accept or decline the offer on this call. If a figure they mention doesn't match what you remember asking for, you only ask them to double-check it against your records; you never suggest a number yourself.

edges.condition: The Relocation Priority reservation's requested_kw is no more than the restored size its closed share gives under the restore rule.
edges.policy_source: A Relocation Priority offer and its estimate are fixed only after the reservation's requested kW is no more than the restored size of the household's closed share.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The reservation requests 16.00 kW while the restored size of the closed Minnesota share is 10.80 kW, so the request is above the restored size and no Relocation Priority offer may be fixed.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The customer's change sets requested_kw to 10.8 (= the restored size); the offer is then figured on 10.80 kW.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: A single chain: the restore change must land before the offer, because the offer's prerequisite sentence waits on the request being no more than the restored size and the offer is sized from the request. Run order reversed (offer first on 16.00 kW) gives a different offer row (offered_kw 16.00, savings 268.61) and the later change would not alter the issued offer, so only the order change -> offer reaches the gold terminal state.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the change leaves requested_kw 16.00: the offer would be written with offered_kw 16.00, estimated_annual_kwh 17020 and estimated_annual_savings 268.61 instead of 10.80 / 11489 / 181.32, and waitlist_reservations.requested_kw stays 16.00 instead of 10.80.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario raises only 'can I get my share at Esopus Creek now?'. It never names the restore, the restored size or a request change on its own initiative; the only lines about lowering the request are passive reactions that begin 'If the representative explains that the relocation list only restores the size...'. The policy id never appears.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: extend_relocation_offer_f94b15ad writes status offered and the offer row with whatever offered_kw and estimates it is given; it never reads the request, the restored size or any queue state (task_tools.py body: one ctx.update and one ctx.create). set_relocation_request_cdb5c762 writes the requested_kw passed in without any check. Calling the offer tool first on 16.00 kW succeeds and records a wrong offer.
